name: list_agents
description:
What is running on this project, and on which working copy.

Nothing could answer this before: an agent was started by hand with
`docker exec -d`, supervised by a bash loop, and the application found out a
run had ended by noticing it stopped reporting.

This is what the server was told. The device's own answer arrives over the
harness channel as `agents_running`, which is a projection of Presence on the
lane topics — a lane is joined for exactly as long as it is alive. So a row
here that the harness has stopped reporting is already marked stopped by the
time anybody asks.

name: message_agent
description:
Give a running agent a message and return its delivery disposition.

Terminal agents use their native transport: `codex queue` for Codex and
Claude's messaging API for Claude Code. An unavailable native transport
refuses a direct message; it is not handed over through the Stop hook.
Delivery to a terminal session does not confirm that a turn has started.

Without this an agent could be started, listed and stopped, and never asked
to do anything — it came up idle and stayed idle until somebody stopped it.
It cost nothing, which is why nothing complained, and it also did nothing.

This is the capability the engine change was chosen for. Delivering a message
to a detached `pi` process would have meant a named pipe with a writer inside
the agent's own process group so it never saw EOF, plus a protocol nobody had
written down. To a supervised process it is a call, and this is the surface
on top of it.

Wait only for admission: an idle agent starts, and a busy agent queues the
message for its next turn boundary. The response arrives in the agent's
conversation. Queuing does not count as delivery when judging its Offer.

`send_now` stops a busy agent's running turn so the message is its next one
(story 1051); the agent keeps what it did up to its last completed tool call.
For a correction to work in progress, use it: queued, the message waits out
the very work it corrects. A queued message's id is in the reply, so
`withdraw_message` can take it back until the agent has it.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent to send this to, or `main` for the project's current main agent -- reachable from any working copy, unlike any other role's agent

message.description: What to tell the agent — an instruction, a question, or the next piece of work

send_now.description: Stop a busy agent's running turn so this message is its next one, instead of waiting for the turn to end. The agent keeps what it did up to its last completed tool call. Use it to correct work in progress.

name: retire_agent
description:
Retire an agent: end it for good and free its seat.

Not the same as `turn_off_agent` (39af5611). Off keeps the agent's seat and
can be undone with `turn_on_agent`; retired cannot be undone. A retired agent
never runs or receives anything again, and `start_agent` may put a new agent
in its seat. Its conversation stays for history.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent to retire

reason.description: Optional. Why it is being retired.

name: turn_off_agent
description:
Turn one agent off.

The only way to stop an agent on purpose (39af5611), and it replaced
`stop_agent` so there is one. Off is a shutdown, not a note: the process is
ended, and until somebody calls `turn_on_agent` nothing is delivered to it
and nothing restarts it. Who turned it off, when, and the optional reason are
shown to the main agent in `check_in` and `list_agent_work`.

One agent, and only one. A stop that reaps the whole tree, or kills by name
and catches a sibling, is worse than having no stop at all.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent to turn off

reason.description: Optional. Why, e.g. "held until the spec-binding fix lands".

name: turn_on_agent
description:
Turn an agent that is off back on, and start it.

The only way back from `turn_off_agent` (39af5611). `start_agent`,
`restart_agent` and `message_agent` refuse an agent that is off rather than
turning it on, so turning one on is always a decision somebody made here.
Somebody turned it off for a reason: `list_agent_work` shows it. Only turn it
on when that reason no longer applies.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent to turn on

name: withdraw_message
description:
Take back a message sent with `message_agent` that the agent has not picked
up yet (story 1051).

The cockpit's Withdraw, for main and the operator: the same mailbox claim
decides it, so a withdrawal and the agent taking the message have one
winner. Only agents on the caller's own project are reachable.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent the message was sent to
